sty2_desc: Teach Appuscholar to write like you. Add your own writing as Word, PDF or text files, or learn from the document you are writing.
sty2_no_project: Open a project to teach Appuscholar your style.
sty2_locked: Your style data is locked. Unlock your vault to read it and use it.
sty2_broken: Your saved style data cannot be opened on this device. Nothing was changed.
sty2_broken_confirm: Saving now replaces what is stored, which cannot be opened. Save anyway?
sty2_own_body: Use text you wrote yourself, without AI and without copying. A published paper by someone else will teach the app their voice, not yours, and passing it off as your style is misuse. Your declaration is saved with this project and appears in your AI-use statement.
sty2_decl: I wrote these samples myself, without AI and without copying from anyone.
sty2_declared_on: declared as my own writing on {date}
sty2_flag: reads differently from your other samples
sty2_flag_note: A flagged file may not be your own writing. If it is not, remove it. If it is, keep it; the flag is a rough guide.
sty2_state_off: Suggestions will not use your style.
sty2_unsaved: You have changes you have not saved.
sty2_ai_profile: The AI wrote the bullet points in this profile from your samples. The last line is measured by code. Read it and change anything that is not you.
sty2_files_hint: Up to {files} files: Word, PDF, text or Markdown. A file over {mb} MB is skipped, and a PDF is read up to {pages} pages.
sty2_studying_files: {files} files read, {words} words. Studying your style.
sty2_learned_doc: Your style is learned. Read the profile and edit it if you like.
sty2_learned_files: Style learned from {files} files ({words} words). Read the profile and edit it if you like.
sty2_skipped: Skipped {n} that could not be read or were too big: {names}.
sty2_full: Your list is full at 100 samples, so the newest was not kept. Remove one to add more.
sty2_need_decl: Tick the box saying this is your own writing first
sty2_need_decl_files: Tick the box saying these files are your own writing first
sty2_need_words: Write at least about {n} words first, then I can learn your style
sty2_few_text_skipped: Could not read enough text. Skipped: {names}
sty2_live_title: Check that the samples are yours: a short typed paraphrase
sty2_live_desc: Read the passage, then write it again in your own words in the box. Pasting is switched off. The app compares your typing with your samples on four habits. It is a rough check, and it cannot prove who wrote anything.
sty2_live_ph: Type your version here (at least 60 words)
sty2_live_few: Type at least 60 words in your own words, then check again.
sty2_live_pasted: Text was inserted by pasting, so it cannot be used. Clear the box and type it.
sty2_live_nosamples: Add at least one sample of 150 words or more first, then check again.
sty2_live_ok: Your typed paraphrase fits your samples on {k} of 4 measures.
sty2_live_partly: Your typed paraphrase fits your samples on only 2 of 4 measures.
sty2_live_differs: Your typed paraphrase differs from your samples on {k} of 4 measures. These may not be one writer. Add more of your own writing, or remove files that are not yours.
sty2_live_foot: This is a rough check. A short text varies a lot, and no tool can prove who wrote something.
sty2_vocab_desc: Choose the meaning of each word, or "I do not know". Ten words give only a rough level. The level keeps suggestions to words you are likely to know. Technical terms of your field stay.
sty2_vocab_result: You answered {k} of 10. Level: {label}. Ten words give only a rough level. Suggestions will use vocabulary at this level, plus words that appear in your own writing, and keep technical terms of your field.
sty2_try_desc: The app writes the practice passage in your learned voice. Judge it.
sty2_try_off: Switch on "Use my style in suggestions" first, so the practice passage is written in your voice.
sty2_try_label: AI wrote this in the voice of your profile. It is a practice paragraph and is not added to your document. Check whether it sounds like you.
sty2_try_ph: What is off? For example: too formal, sentences too long
sty2_erase_confirm: Erase your samples, profile, declaration and vocabulary result?
sty2_vo4_0: Open to more than one meaning
sty2_vo9_0: Done as a duty with little effort
sty2_passage_0: Many students believe that studying late into the night helps them remember more, but the evidence points the other way. Sleep gives the brain time to sort what it has learned and to store the important parts. A student who sleeps well before an examination usually recalls facts faster and makes fewer careless mistakes than a student who stayed awake to revise one more chapter.
sty2_passage_1: A quiet library is often praised as the best place to study, yet some students work better with a little background noise. A café, a corridor or a shared room can hold attention for people who find silence tiring. The useful question is not which place is best for everyone, but which place lets a particular student keep working for an hour without drifting.
sty2_passage_2: Group study can help when each member prepares alone first and then explains the topic to the others. Explaining forces a student to find the gaps in their own understanding. It helps much less when the group meets only to copy notes, because nobody then has to put an idea into their own words, and the sense of progress is greater than the progress itself.
